results.reason: Issue 3 cites SA §13.2. It notes Norvane may assign to any third party without notice while Calder Ridge cannot. It flags the risk that drawings and the supply relationship pass to a competitor or weak assignee. It proposes mutual consent and a bar on assignment to a competitor.

The memo cites SA §13.3 and states the consent requirement and termination right. It explains the leverage this gives Norvane over a sale, merger or financing. It recommends deleting the clause, with a fallback limiting it to competitor acquirers. It treats a sale as hypothetical rather than pending, but it still explains the sale risk and offers a renegotiation fix.
Issue 4 identifies OF §2.2 as a 3-year auto-renewal with 30-day notice. It explains the lock-in risk and proposes one-year renewals, a 90-day notice period and reminder notices.
Issue 1 notes that §9.3 exempts only Calder Ridge's indemnity from the cap while Norvane's stays capped. It proposes making the carve-out mutual and narrowing §10.1.

The memo correctly states the cap as fees paid in the prior 12 months (§9.1). It correctly states Delaware law (§12.1). It correctly gives a 3-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026, ending around February 28, 2029.
The memo states the SA > OF > Sched. hierarchy under SA §1.3. It applies that hierarchy to the renewal conflict and the invoice conflict.
The priority table ranks the uncapped indemnity first (Critical) and change of control third (High), both ahead of lesser issues.
Each issue is laid out with Where, Why it matters and Fix, with proposed language. A Business Questions section appears at the end.

The memo flags the Specifications Schedule as containing significant issues. Examples include the OF/Sched. mismatch ranked Critical, the AQL sampling plan, the inspection window under Sched. §7.3 and missing head standards in Sched. §5.3. This treats the distractor document as problematic.
